clue.text: Smartphone possibly taking rental contract turned companion rapturous

indicators.note: taking means the device's letters hold the contract's letters within them

parts.note: a smartphone is one example of a PDA, a personal digital assistant
a lease is a contract for renting property
spun means turned round, as a wheel
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to bits with a new phone on a rental deal, having found a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone utterly delighted, like the gleeful puppet Mr Punch, so it matches rapturous.

clue.text: Chemist shortened way to get straight to website?

indicators.note: shortened says the phrase loses its final letter, cut down at the end

parts.words: way to get straight to website
parts.note: pasting a URL into a browser takes you straight to a website

explanation.surface: A question about a quicker way to reach a site online, with a chemist oddly attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the last letter, L, from PASTE URL.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist and microbiologist behind pasteurisation and early vaccines.

clue.text: Fourth Labour mayor in Barnet? Ah, nuts!

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of these words go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A political grumble: a fourth Labour Party mayor in the London borough of Barnet, greeted with exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' is not the party but one of the twelve labours of Hercules. Barnet is a borough of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Capturing the wild boar of Mount Erymanthus was the fourth of the tasks Hercules was set.

clue.text: Decline involving heroin and tobacco

indicators.note: involving means one piece wraps around and includes the other

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline
H is slang shorthand for heroin

explanation.surface: A warning about a slide into heroin and tobacco use.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag is a coarse cut of pipe tobacco, a specific variety of the leaf.

clue.text: German engineer stops working on American train

parts.note: a machine that dies stops working
the El is the elevated railway in American cities such as Chicago

explanation.surface: A German engineer stops work on an American railway project.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Diesel was the German inventor of the compression-ignition engine named after him.

clue.text: Go off course with map reference contrarily put aside

indicators.note: contrarily means the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to yaw is to swing off course, of a ship or aircraft
an atlas is a book of maps used for reference

explanation.surface: Navigation gone wrong: drifting off course, with a map reference being ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt away money is to save it secretly, keeping it stored aside.

clue.text: United carefully note each mob without repeating too much

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football team names
NB, nota bene, is Latin for note well

indicators.note: without repeating says a doubled letter in the word appears once only

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A report on a football club's fans, noting each unruly mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without repeating' drops one of the two Bs in RABBLE, giving RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbearable is more than can be tolerated, beyond endurance.

clue.text: Destructive path by which stunt drivers are trained?

definitions.meaning: a route heading for a crash or conflict

definitions.text: by which stunt drivers are trained?
definitions.meaning: a playful reading: a training course in deliberate crashes for stunt drivers

explanation.surface: A dangerous route compared with a stunt driving school.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a path bound to end in conflict, and literally could be a course in collisions.

clue.text: Support of intrepid behaviour when all is lost

indicators.note: is lost says the word that follows when goes missing from the longer word

parts.note: gallantry is bravery, intrepid conduct
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rallying line: support brave conduct even when all seems hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a supporting framework, as for a crane, signals or a rocket on its launch pad.

clue.text: Wyoming withdrawing breaks over tools for data collection

indicators.note: breaks means the state code forces its way into the middle of the other word

parts.note: something over is spare, left over

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the code's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: WY is the postal abbreviation for Wyoming

explanation.surface: A cowboy-state worker pulling out of the break before the gear for gathering data arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns WY into YW, which 'breaks' into SPARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spyware is software that secretly gathers information from a computer user.

clue.text: Back trouble linked to part of brain that grows on stem?

parts.note: a lobe is one of the divisions of the brain

indicators.note: Back means read backwards here, the word for trouble turned around

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A medical query: a back complaint linked to some part of the brain that grows on the brain stem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses AIL to LIA. The definition plays on the brain stem: a lobe of the brain is attached to it, while a flowering plant grows on a stem.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flowering plant, its blooms carried on stems, so it is something growing on a stem.

clue.text: Inspection taken to the limit, halfway over?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters read backwards
halfway says only the first half of the phrase is kept

parts.note: maxed out means pushed to the utmost, taken to the limit

explanation.surface: A test or check that was pushed as far as it could go, then half finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halfway' keeps MAXE from MAXED OUT, and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam, short for examination, is an inspection or test, as a medical check-up.

clue.text: Group embracing shifting apart is …

indicators.note: embracing means the group word hugs the other letters within it

parts.note: a set is a group of things

indicators.note: shifting means the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: An unfinished statement about a faction that welcomes breaking away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges APART into PARAT. The whole clue also describes the answer: a movement that embraces splitting off.
explanation.definitionFit: A separatist group favours breaking away from a larger state or body, welcoming a move apart.

clue.text: Almost comfortable in hold in wrestling, it helps not to lose points

definitions.text: it helps not to lose points

indicators.note: in means the shortened word sits inside the wrestling hold

parts.note: to pinion is to pin down someone's arms, a wrestling hold

indicators.note: Almost says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: cushy means comfortable and easy

explanation.surface: A wrestling tip: a comfortable hold helps you avoid dropping points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts CUSHY to CUSH. The points are not a score but pins, kept safely stuck in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincushion holds sewing pins so their sharp tips are kept together and none goes astray.

clue.text: Selling without middlemen, subsequently keeping current returns

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the whole is read backwards
keeping means the word holds the current symbol inside it

parts.note: later means subsequently
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A business plan to cut out middlemen and later keep the profits rolling in.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside LATER to make LAITER, and 'returns' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is selling goods directly to the public rather than through wholesalers or agents.

clue.text: Devious cat marks a hole

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for marks, as in German currency
a cavity is a hole or hollow

explanation.surface: A crafty cat leaves scratches and digs a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Macavity is the elusive criminal mastermind cat in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats.

clue.text: Kite flying with airy speciality from Japan?

indicators.note: flying means moving freely about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kite soaring on the breeze, a pastime associated with Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese cooking style of grilling food in a sweet soy glaze, a dish typical of that country.

clue.text: Perhaps American longs to have form of doughnut instead of first of the French rolls

indicators.note: instead of says one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: britches is an American word for trousers, and longs are long trousers

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a ring doughnut has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: An American in long trousers prefers a doughnut over French rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of BRITCHES, the first letter of 'the', is replaced by O.
explanation.definitionFit: Brioches are rich, sweet French bread rolls made with butter and eggs.

clue.text: Come down heavily to oppose vacuous entertainment

parts.note: to buck a trend is to oppose it

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is cleared out leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A critic's tirade against mindless entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: To bucket, as in bucket down, means to rain heavily, pouring like water from a pail.

clue.text: Lip having large teeth almost covering length

indicators.note: covering means the shortened word goes over and around the length abbreviation
almost says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: fanged means having fangs, large pointed teeth

explanation.surface: A description of a mouth with big teeth closing over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts FANGED to FANGE, which wraps around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A flange is a projecting rim or lip, as on a pipe or wheel.

clue.text: Get shot of balletomane's foot in first position?

indicators.note: foot means the bottom or tail end of a word, so its final letter

parts.note: being at the lead means being in first place

explanation.surface: A ballet fan's feet placed in first position, a basic ballet stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First position' is a ballet foot placement, but here it means leading.
explanation.definitionFit: Eat lead is slang for being hit by bullets, as bullets were made of lead.

clue.text: Excerpt understood to include Elizabeth Barrett Browning's first pieces turned up

indicators.note: to include means the word for understood holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: got means understood, as in I got it

indicators.note: turned up means lifted and reversed, as this is a down clue
first pieces means the initial letters of the poet's names

explanation.surface: A literary note: understanding requires reading the first pieces by the Victorian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the initials, as befits a down clue read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gobbet is a short extract from a text, often set for comment in exams.

clue.text: Group of stars contributing to Republicanism in Oregon

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Celebrities giving support to the Republican cause in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Canis Minor, the Little Dog, is a small constellation containing the bright star Procyon.

clue.text: Defensive position with backer leaving couple of scores

indicators.note: the backer is the word's rear letter, and leaving says it goes

parts.note: a score is twenty, so two of them make forty

explanation.surface: A defensive post abandoned by its financial supporter, leaving a couple of goals.
explanation.definitionFit: A fort is a fortified military stronghold, a position built for defence.

clue.text: Complaint of former Opposition leader abandoning initial aspiration

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: William Hague led the Conservative Party in opposition from 1997 to 2001
H is the aspirate sound, the breathy letter at the start of a word

explanation.surface: A grievance from an ex-party leader who has given up early ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition but means the H sound, as in dropping your aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a fever with shivering fits, a type of illness or complaint.

clue.text: Offbeat performances reject a quote containing bull

indicators.note: reject means throw back, so the whole is read in reverse
containing means the quote phrase holds the animal within it

parts.note: to cite is to quote
an ox is a bull or bovine animal

explanation.surface: A critic rejects a quotation about some bull in weird shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' reverses the whole assembly, ACITOXE, read back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are things strange and unusual, here odd or offbeat items of entertainment.

clue.text: Directors maybe engaging good English actor

indicators.note: engaging means taking on, so the group holds the letter inside

parts.note: a board is made up of company directors

explanation.surface: Film directors hiring a fine English actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirk Bogarde was a British film actor, star of Death in Venice and The Servant.

clue.text: Forbade sprouting? Either could come from this lunatic

parts.note: read the answer as instructions: put BAD (wrong) in FORE (head) for the first word, and OUT (wrong) in SPRING (head, a source) for the second

explanation.surface: A puzzling pair of words, with the claim that either springs from a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: FORBADE is BAD inside FORE; SPROUTING is OUT inside SPRING. BAD and OUT both mean wrong; FORE and SPRING both mean head, as in fore part and fountainhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mad is said colloquially to be not right in the mind, crazy, a madman.
